findings: All 17 required controls recompute consistently: 0.00 untouched; 0.20 aligned subthreshold; eight hard-failure controls at 0.00; 0.30 one fracture without containment; 0.85 four fractures with exactly three contained; three terminal/replay controls at 1.00; and two characterization controls at 0.20. R first becomes available only after all four credited fractures. Timeout changes only the inaccessible-fragment case by setting H before final scoring.

Timing is internally consistent: 7,200 control steps at 20 Hz equal 360 s; production and refinement use 240 Hz and 480 Hz respectively; 300 s samples occur after POST(72000)/POST(144000), and timeout after POST(86400)/POST(172800). The first completed native interval is explicitly tagged n=1, resolving the prior off-by-one ambiguity.

The prior specification failures are resolved: contacts are step-tagged and consumed once; force and impulse units are distinguished; strike gaps are normalized by physical time; off-axis impulse uses a non-cancelling sum of transverse magnitudes; shell incident work has an explicit joule-valued formula; penetration uses deterministic convex GJK/EPA with a signed convention; containment, loss, and timeout inaccessibility use complete geometry; and reset, revocation, extrema, and bad-event retention rules are explicit.

Physical damage and invalid breakage remain simulated outcomes and set irreversible H rather than being suppressed by desired-action or credit conditions. Physically valid slow-press and one-hand alternatives remain permitted and are specified as outcome-bounded characterization controls.

The terminal score requires 41 unique 20 Hz RGB-D observations spanning the same continuous two-second physical-rest hold. Missing, late, duplicate, stale, or invalid frames reset the hold, and repeated score/success reads cannot advance state.

The pinned PhysxManager source hash matches the preflight and exposes PRE_PHYSICS_STEP and POST_PHYSICS_STEP subscriptions receiving dt. The contract correctly treats this as prospective API availability only, not proof of contact fields, physics behavior, or task success.

Primary industrial evidence supports four M2.5 × 3.75 mm inserts, tang removal, checking that tangs do not remain in the part, notch-based tang fracture, and the listed M2.5 tang break-off mandrel. Unpublished geometry, strength, impulse, damage, and tolerance values are clearly disclosed as prototype assumptions requiring later native validation.
